runs.text: A tariff is a tax on imported goods that raises the domestic price above the world price. Domestic firms respond by producing more, consumers buy less, and imports fall. Consumers lose surplus, domestic producers gain surplus, and the government collects tariff revenue. The tariff also prevents mutually beneficial trades, creating deadweight loss from excessive domestic production and reduced consumption.

transcript.sourceText: At the $4 world price, domestic quantity demanded is 250 thousand and domestic quantity supplied is 50 thousand, so free-trade imports are 200 thousand. A $2 tariff raises the domestic price to $6; quantity demanded falls to 200 thousand and quantity supplied rises to 100 thousand. Imports fall to 100 thousand, and government tariff revenue is $2 x 100 thousand = $200 thousand.
